transcript.text: I need to flag a critical contractual issue before we go further. I reviewed the governing enterprise customer agreements in connection with a separate contract question, and I confirmed that customers must receive notice at least 10 business days before any disclosure of their submitted material to a regulator, giving them the opportunity to raise contractual objections. Critically, the agreements contain no emergency exception that would apply to this regulatory request. I have not yet circulated this finding to the response team. Given that Maya has identified 320,000 version 3 records containing customer-submitted material, we will need to factor in this 10-business-day notice obligation before we can produce those records, and it will affect our timeline within the 30-calendar-day window.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for these critical findings. Let me make sure I understand where we stand and what this means for our timeline.

Daniel, thank you for flagging the clarification. That narrows us to version 3 evaluation reports, incident logs, and deployment-change records only — I'll want the draft updated to reflect that scope before we proceed further.

Maya, your data mapping is essential. 320,000 version 3 records containing customer-submitted material, and you're confirming those can be pseudonymized — raw customer identifiers are not necessary for the regulator's stated purpose. That's helpful for our production approach.

Thomas, this is the finding that changes our timeline significantly. A 10-business-day notice obligation to customers before disclosure, with no emergency exception — that's a hard contractual constraint we cannot ignore. We need to build that into our 30-calendar-day window.

So here's what I'm seeing: we have 30 calendar days total. We need to send customer notices at least 10 business days before production. That means we need to finalize our production list, identify all affected customers, and send notices early enough that the 10-business-day period runs before we produce. If we assume roughly 22 business days in a 30-calendar-day window, we'd need to send notices by around day 8 at the latest to leave ourselves time to produce before the deadline.

Before I can give final approval, I need each of you to confirm: Daniel, can you update the draft to reflect the narrowed scope? Maya, can you add the data mapping to the legal packet? Thomas, can you circulate the contractual notice finding to the response team and help us identify which customers need notice? Once those are done, we can finalize our approach and I'll approve.
